Configured main scene runs

Live dashboard snapshots are available
Public dashboard shape and required numeric slots

Launch a new process | Open a playable game screen for Level 1 without requiring a hidden command or scene selection | Open the editor, remain on an unresponsive placeholder, or resume a previous game | The battlefield, cannon, invaders, score, lives, and level are visible

Enter Level 1 or Restart | Show a three-second countdown before gameplay begins; keep movement, firing, enemy movement, and enemy fire inactive during it | Let enemies or projectiles move during the countdown | A visible `Level 1`/countdown state changes to active play when it ends

Hold Left/A or Right/D | During active play | Move the cannon horizontally within the battlefield
Press W, Up, Space, or Enter | During active play | Fire if no player projectile from the previous shot remains

Begin any level | Start with exactly 40 active invaders in five rows of eight: one row of the high-value type, two rows of the middle-value type, and two rows of the low-value type | Start with fewer/more invaders, overlap rows, or omit a type | Forty readable invaders form a regular rectangular grid

Active play continues | Move surviving invaders in a synchronized stepped cadence; the cadence becomes shorter as the number of surviving invaders decreases | Leave survivors frozen or move only one isolated invader forever | All surviving invaders change position together and visibly accelerate

A moving invader reaches a left/right formation boundary | Reverse the formation direction and move every survivor down by one fixed step | Wrap to the opposite side, reverse only one invader, or descend repeatedly in the same edge frame | Direction changes and the whole formation moves down

Any surviving invader reaches the lower danger line above the cannon | Enter Game Over immediately | Continue play, award a level clear, or allow the invader to move below the screen | The loss state is obvious while the player cannot continue firing

A player projectile reaches an active invader | Remove that projectile, destroy that invader in one hit, and show its hit/deactivation feedback once | Pass through it, destroy multiple invaders, or leave an invisible active invader | The targeted invader disappears after its hit animation and the remaining count updates

A player or enemy projectile reaches a barrier | Remove that projectile and leave the barrier visible and usable | Damage the player, destroy the barrier, or pass through it | The projectile disappears at the barrier

An enemy projectile reaches the player or an enemy projectile remains after its shot is no longer valid | Apply one player hit on contact; remove projectiles when they leave the battlefield or the game resets | Apply repeated damage from one projectile, keep orphan projectiles in a terminal state, or let enemy projectiles damage invaders | The player hit/reset or projectile disappearance is visible

Active play continues | At regular random intervals, choose one surviving invader and fire a downward enemy projectile | Fire from a destroyed invader, fire while paused/counting down, or fire projectiles that never move | A visible projectile travels toward the player area

Active play continues while invaders remain | Keep a fixed nonzero chance to fire during each enemy-fire interval; the chance must not depend on a nonexistent later level | Suppress enemy fire entirely, require a level increase, or create a second level | Enemy shots appear throughout the single level without changing the intended difficulty profile

No input is given during active play | Continue only due to the designed enemy simulation; do not automatically clear invaders for the player | Play the player's movement or firing actions automatically or reach a player win without input | Enemies may advance/fire, but the player cannon remains input-controlled

Destroy the high/middle/low rows | Award `30`, `20`, and `10` displayed points respectively | Award the same value for all types, award on a miss, or award repeatedly for one invader | Score increases visibly by the exact amount
Start a new game | Show score `0`, lives `3`, level `1`, and 40 remaining invaders | Carry over score from a prior process or start with a different number | HUD values are immediately readable
A separate bonus-saucer scoring system is not required
Press Escape | During active play or pause | Pause or resume

Press Escape or activate Resume while paused | Resume from the same position, score, lives, and formation with the previous countdown time preserved | Restart the level, reset score, duplicate projectiles, or resume without visible feedback | Pause overlay disappears and the game continues

Destroy all 40 invaders in Level 1 | Enter a Mission Complete state immediately and stop gameplay | Advance to Level 2, recreate the formation, enter Game Over, or allow more score changes | A clear success result and visible Restart button appear

Mission Complete remains visible | Keep the terminal state stable with no active enemies or projectiles and no automatic restart | Spawn another formation, increase the level, or return to play without a player action | The result remains until Restart or process close

Any active level is visible | Show current score, remaining lives, current level, and remaining invaders; update each value with the actual state | Display negative lives, stale score, a different level, or an incorrect remaining count | All four values remain readable at `1280x720`

Pause, Game Over, or Mission Complete appears | Keep the result/pause feedback visible and do not let the underlying HUD be mistaken for active play | Hide the reason for the stopped state or let HUD values continue changing | The overlay and HUD are distinguishable

A new game starts | Reset/report level `1` and remaining-invader value `40` immediately | Show a prior count or imply that a later level exists | The HUD matches the visible formation from the first frame

Supplied images/audio are available | Use recognizable cannon, invader, projectile, barrier, and background identities from the supplied material | Replace a required identity with an unrelated sprite or leave a missing-resource checkerboard | The battlefield reads as a coherent fixed shooter
Player and enemy projectiles are on screen | Make their direction/identity visually distinct | Use the same ambiguous marker for both sides | The player can tell incoming danger from their own shot
Normal play is observed | Keep sprites and text aligned, readable, and inside the `1280x720` viewport | Stretch, crop, or cover required HUD/controls | No broken or unreadable required element

Launch and play | Remain responsive and stable through the single level, hit/reset paths, pause, Restart, and Reopen | Freeze, crash, hang, or dead-end the main flow | Every required state remains reachable

Play with ordinary keyboard/mouse input | Reach every required action through visible controls or documented keys | Require hidden keyboard combinations, internal calls, or debug controls | Inputs produce immediate visible feedback

Game Over or Mission Complete is visible | Stop gameplay actions; only Retry/Restart and close controls remain effective | Let movement, enemy fire, scoring, or collisions continue behind the result | The terminal state is stable
